messages.subject: Re: likelihood
messages.body_plain:
Xinya,

The information criteria are generally marginal, but you can get conditional by adding the argument "save.lvs=TRUE" to the model estimation command. Then some new metrics will appear in fitMeasures(), with "_cond" in their name. (And note that marginal are generally recommended.)

Ed

messages.subject: Re: likelihood
messages.body_plain:
Xinya,

The latent variables are assumed to come from a normal distribution, which is the same as non-Bayesian SEM. We might call the latent variable distribution a "hyperdistribution". Then, in a Bayesian model, the free parameters of the hyperdistribution (mean or variance of the normal distribution) would receive prior distributions. Those prior distributions can be found in dpriors().

Ed

messages.subject_clean: lambda: Loading parameters. & rho: Correlation parameters (associated with covariance parameters).
messages.body_plain:
Hao,

lambda are the factor loadings, whereas "rho" is only used when we decompose a covariance matrix. For example, sometimes we take the residual covariance matrix (often called Theta) and decompose it into

Theta = D Rho D,

where D is a diagonal matrix of residual standard deviations and Rho is a correlation matrix (contains correlations between residual terms). Then the prior distribution for entries of Rho comes from the "rho" part of dpriors(). Technical details can be found here:

https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v085.i04

For your 1-factor model, the rho priors are not used. So your fit1 and fit3 should be the same model (lambda priors specified in two different ways), while fit2 just uses the default prior for lambda (dnorm(0,1e-2)). But the fit3 specification is a little funny because you have a prior on all three loadings, but the first loading is typically fixed to 1 for identification.

Ed
